Digital twins to simulate and improve your plant

Digital twins are exact virtual replicas of your physical operations. They allow you to simulate process changes, test improvements, or predict outcomes without halting production.

This technology helps reduce risks and accelerates innovation: for example, a factory can virtually test a new machine configuration or workflow change before implementing it in real life, saving time and costs.

Problems it solves

  • Process changes that can only be tested by stopping the line.
  • Machinery investments decided without knowing where the bottleneck is.
  • Production planning done with spreadsheets and gut feeling.
  • Difficulty predicting the effect of a change in product, shift pattern or demand.

How we do it

  1. We narrow down the question to answer: capacity, bottlenecks, energy use or quality.
  2. We model the process with its real data: cycle times, stoppages, changeovers and material flows.
  3. We validate the twin against the plant's actual behaviour.
  4. We simulate scenarios with your team and measure their effect before anything is changed.
  5. Where it makes sense, we connect the twin to live data so it tracks what is happening in the plant.

Example applications

  • Testing a new machine layout or a change in workflow.
  • Sizing a line or warehouse extension.
  • Estimating the impact of a shift change or a demand peak.
  • Finding the configuration that cuts energy use without losing output.

Frequently asked questions

What is a digital twin?

It is a virtual model of a machine, line or plant that behaves like the real one because it is fed with its data. It is used to test changes and predict outcomes without stopping production.

Does the plant need to be fully instrumented?

Not to get started. A first twin can be built from historical production data, with live data added later.

How long does it take to build a digital twin?

It depends on the scope. We recommend starting with one line or process and extending it once it is delivering results.
